title: We launched our AI-assisted game on Youtube after 4 months of careful refinement and here is what we used
author: hyperg8_games
selftext:
Today our Megaman 2-7 inspired oldschool 3d action platformer game got finally released on Youtube Playables and it was a long path to get there.

  
**;tl:dr;** 4 month to get from initial draft to a finished product that has its gameplay and onboarding optimized after real player playtest on Poki gave our feedback to bugfix, but most of all give inspiration of putting carrots along the players path, so the player does not get bored.   
We were able to raise Mega Droids **from 3.5 minutes to 6.5 minutes** average playtime from the first draft to the currently released version. We released [***Mega Droid on Youtube Playables***](https://youtube.com/playables/UgkxorjaigG47LgUlJBIiQxuDxiXhQRoh5IF?si=TQjxGPMshdcDOnKG)***.***



The development started in July on a rough idea about a ***casual*** game inspired by **MegaMan-like** blaster arm robot that traverses platformer levels with strong boss fights that makes you think about which weapon to use, to experiment with different special weapons and a high emphasis on perfect play with parry and perfectly timed charge shots and taking cover from boss attacks behind pillars.

The mission design was highly inspired by the **Elder Scrolls: Blades** mobile game and therefore the whole game was optimized for weak mobile devices (*device target audience Argentina, Brazil, Mexico*). The whole game was designed as a casual web game and not for 1+ hour sessions like a normal Steam game.

After drafting the first version of the Game Design Document with the *toon art style* and the futuristic UI requirements and the above mentioned game design, we started the first **Claude Code Opus 5.1** implementation of Mega Droid. The world and the characters and animations are all Claude generated, but thats not a bit issue, since *complex animations and high poly models would have broken our fps budget anyways.*

The result was good for a first draft, it had the toon look, a very basic level layout ála ES: Blades, the charged shot and super shitty AI sounds, but a quite nice ambient city skyline that catches the players eyes on the first entry.

Playtesting the first version with 4 different enemy types already was fun, as it had 3 iconic Megaman alike enemy machines that transfered a cute look on machines and robots, we were excited to make this into something exciting, the basis was there and it showed great potential.

But that was only the beginning and the game had no chance to succeed at that point!

  
1 month later after refining platformer levels, adding bosses and voice-overs, we dared to start our first playtests to find out if this game had a chance at becomming successful by running Poki Playtests with video recordings.  
Luckily we aquired a brand new developer access to **Pokis Playtesting tools** and that was an absolute game changer for our web game studio, it offered us free video recording to every game we had in development and a quick test to find out where the main visual and gameplay hurdles in the game are.  
The very first playtests were already promising, with an **average playtime of 3.5 minutes** on a very short lived audience (Poki players generally *play 6-15 minutes per session* or game and on average max 30 minutes per session, of cause there are outliers).

  
So we went back to refining the gameplay and sounds and VOs and added a story arc with new voice-overs, an thematic intro that shows the player capabilities in a short cutscene and most importantly a guided tutorial with holograms, which show the players capabilities and which keys and buttons to press.

  
Skipping 3 months forward we have been able to improve our average playtime on Poki playtests from 3.5 minutes to 6.5 minutes, just by throwing in something new and interesting to find stuff and explore and giving the player a guided game experience without leaving the player being lost.  
**This is game design in it's core** and is not something you can draft in your initial GDD, since this is not the thing that you think about when imagining a world, but in the end: That is what makes a game interesting to play and not just a chore to try to find out the games mechanics.

  
We launched the game on Playgama (a casual web game platform) last month and the game got an average of \~11 minutes play sessions on Playgama playerbase, which was enough to qualify for Youtube Playables.

Today we are finally releasing the game on Youtube Playables, our prime web game platform target with a decent average playtime and a high D1 retention values recorded from Playgama Dashboard metrics.

The covers have been created with **Geminis Nano Banana** within multiple hundert of iterations.

If you want to check out the [***Mega Droid on Youtube Playables***](https://youtube.com/playables/UgkxorjaigG47LgUlJBIiQxuDxiXhQRoh5IF?si=TQjxGPMshdcDOnKG):   
[https://youtube.com/playables/UgkxorjaigG47LgUlJBIiQxuDxiXhQRoh5IF?si=TQjxGPMshdcDOnKG](https://youtube.com/playables/UgkxorjaigG47LgUlJBIiQxuDxiXhQRoh5IF?si=TQjxGPMshdcDOnKG)
